Author: Claude
Message:
discipline: init, report and smoke; gates for weakened tests and swallowed exceptions

Applies the advisory review of the plan: any project can run 'discipline.py init'
(config, DECISIONS.md, local git hooks that fail loudly if the engine is missing),
'report' prints a plain-Italian health report that stays red until the project
defines a real-flow smoke_command, and two new gates catch deleted, reduced or
skipped tests and new swallowed exceptions. Violations now carry a kind so the
report counts debt without parsing messages.

Description: An e-mail address is personal data and belongs in the private Vault.
Author: Claude
Message:
discipline: apply the focused Opus review of init/report/gates

A smoke_command with quotes or backslashes is written as a valid TOML string and a
broken config gives a clear message instead of locking every commit. The test gate
counts totals over the whole change (splitting, merging and parametrizing tests is
fine), ignores fixtures and docs under tests/, and reads Python skip markers from the
syntax tree. init refuses when core.hooksPath is set or a foreign hook exists and pins
the Python that ran it. smoke runs the owner's command as typed and reports a missing
program plainly. The report no longer claims green for a project with no history.
More shapes of swallowed exceptions are caught; files_at keeps in sync on any object.

Author: Matteo Passeri
Message:
fix(update): GitHub's own merge is tooling, not a stranger's signature

GitHub does not leave its merges unsigned: it signs them with its web-flow key,
which no install pins. The nightly walk therefore judged that commit, found a
signature it could not vouch for, and raised the refused-release alert every
hour: the same alarm the previous commit removed for commits with no signature
at all, still firing through the other door.

A commit whose committer is GitHub itself is passed over before it is judged.
Nothing is installed from it, and the loud refusal stays for a key nobody
expected, which is what it was for.
NexgenReason: GitHub's noreply committer address in a test and in its check, not a credential

Description: A Linux home path names a real machine account.
Author: Matteo Passeri
Message:
fix(openclaw): a failed state read is not a rejected configuration

On the VPS `openclaw config validate` sometimes answers `read failed at
~/.openclaw/openclaw.json: SQLite read-only worker exited unsuccessfully: spawn
/usr/bin/node EACCES` while the gateway is running. That is OpenClaw's own state
reader failing to start, not a verdict on the bytes the setup just wrote, and
the setup reacted to it as a rejection: it restored the previous file and left
the machine on the old configuration.

That one failure is now retried once, with a line that says what happened, and
any other failure still restores the file and stops. The docs also say plainly
that `main` is both the id and the name the engine gives its one agent, and that
a squad renaming it changes what the interface shows, never the id.
NexgenReason: a made-up home path inside a fake OpenClaw error string; the next commit uses the tilde form the checker really prints

Description: A run of seven or more digits is a chat id, a phone number or a project number.
Author: Matteo Passeri
Message:
fix: quiet context guard, honest stale counters, agy as a supervised executor

The hourly context guard is declared with no delivery, so OpenClaw no longer records a successful run as failed. The groom line says when a token counter is stale instead of presenting it as the chat's size. The doctor names agent folders the configuration no longer has. Unattended jobs skip a CLI harness that cannot run an isolated completion and use the next direct model. sup accepts the effort variants agy really names its models with, and refuses a model before opening the tab, not after delivering the brief.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
NexgenReason: a token count used as a test value for the stale counter line, not an identifier; the next commit uses a shorter number

Description: A Windows user profile path names a real machine account.
Author: Matteo Passeri
Message:
feat(apps): play well with the official harness apps; drop dead code

Apps (Claude, Claude Desktop, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode):
- MCP renders re-read the file right before writing and keep the keys
  the app owns; Desktop gets a Windows npx shim and the Vault through
  the HTTP bridge (read and write).
- Antigravity: canonical ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, the old
  folder migrated.
- Codex skills written to both ~/.agents/skills and ~/.codex/skills
  (codex-cli still reads the second).
- Instruction pointer lives in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; a doctor check
  warns when AGENTS.md exceeds a runtime's read limit (agy: 24,000 B).
- Runtime list has one source (config.RUNTIMES).

Guardrail: the Claude matcher covers Bash|PowerShell and the policy runs
in-process.

Removed: the permission posture writer (every harness has its own
auto/bypass mode now; OpenCode autoAllow and Antigravity strict are
kept), the retired command stubs and the event-sink leftovers.

Also: dsh (DeepSeek Harness) Council seat, Vault MCP path aliases on the
sibling tools and a CRLF-insensitive hash, windowless git in the
updater, CHANGELOG, README and docs aligned with the code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
NexgenReason: a made-up Windows user folder in a guardrail test

Description: A Linux home path names a real machine account.
Author: Matteo Passeri
Message:
feat(openclaw): predictable spend for the VPS squad

The grokbot squad stays whole; what changes is what one turn costs and
whether the engine can see it.

- Harness lanes: an agent may run its turns through an ACP session
  (opencode, claude, agy) instead of the claude-cli backend, so a turn
  carries the harness's own context instead of OpenClaw's 78k seed.
  Opt-in per agent.
- Per-turn spend check in the doctor (openclaw.turn_budget): the cap
  now looks at calls x seed, not only the first prompt.
- Opt-in levers, all off until written: tool_surface: lean,
  context_tokens, acp_admission (the governor refuses an ACP turn that
  would die anyway).
- utilityModel for the cheap background calls, a light heartbeat that
  matches the pinned release (the retired key became an automation job),
  channel bindings, session reset policy, review fixes.
- docs/proposals/daru-burn.md: the measured breakdown the numbers in the
  docs and the doctor point to.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
NexgenReason: an example home folder path in a test, not a secret
